body:
emily.chen: Heads-up — customer's POC failing on structured output when we enable streaming + tool calls. Repro steps in thread. raj.patel: Oof. Which customer and model/endpoint? :thinking_face: emily.chen: AcmeFin, using hosted /v1/chat.completions -> model redwood-xy-2-large. They want a tool_call to run a policy-checker and then return a strict JSON document. Works fine w/o stream, fails when stream=true. marco_dev: Can you paste the raw stream log? Might be interleaved chunks from tool output. emily.chen: Paste below (sanitized): ``` [stream chunk] {"role":"tool","name":"policy_check","content":"{\"status\":\"ok\",\"details\":\"passed\"}"} [stream chunk] {"role":"assistant","content":"\nNote: policy passed — embedding results follow"} [stream chunk] {"role":"assistant","content":"\n{\"result\":{\"score\":0.98}}"} [stream done] ``` sara_ops: I think the assistant inserted an extra plain-text comment into the JSON stream between tool chunks, so the final assembled payload isn't valid JSON. raj.patel: That matches our customer's error: "JSONDecodeError: Extra data". They expect a single JSON object produced by the assistant after the tool returns — streaming breaks the envelope. emily.chen: They hit this when we have both streaming and function/tool calling enabled. Works reliably if stream=false. But streaming is required for their latency SLAs. marco_dev: Two things to consider: 1) runtime should emit tool call content as a single atomic chunk or mark tool boundaries, 2) provide a strict-json flag that ensures assistant can't emit free text when JSON mode is requested. deploy-bot: deploy status: candidate patch for streaming framing queued to eng-runtime CI. Build #4892 started. raj.patel: Customer also asked about pricing for Dedicated POC (4x A100 equivalent) and an urgent QSA for their security questionnaire. Can we answer both while we triage? :grimacing: emily.chen: Pricing note: we can offer a 30-day Dedicated eval credit — I'll confirm numbers but need capacity ops approval. QSA: they sent pack with SOC2 + encryption questions; security expects us to reply but asked for product contact. sara_ops: Back to the technical POC — error stack they get: ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "app.py", line 213, in handle_response parsed = json.loads(stream_assembled) json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 1 column 215 (char 214) ``` marco_dev: Can you include the exact chunks with separators? If tool content is emitted as role=tool then role=assistant commentary inserted between streaming chunks, then the final concatenation is invalid. Possible workaround: have the SDK assemble only content from `role":"assistant"` messages that follow end_of_tool_call marker. emily.chen: Customer tried that — they filter to last assistant chunk after tool call end, but sometimes middleware inserts newlines and the assistant opens a new JSON object rather than continuing the one. raj.patel: Is there a simple prompt-level mitigation? E.g., tell the model: "When using stream=true and a tool returns, emit exactly one JSON object and no extra commentary."? marco_dev: Prompt trick: wrap with system message: "OUTPUT_FORMAT: STRICT_JSON — you must output only a single top-level JSON object. If you need to explain, call the debug_tool instead." But we shouldn't rely on heuristics for enterprise POCs. sara_ops: Eng request: is there a runtime flag to enforce "json_mode":strict? We'd prefer an SDK/runtime-side validation that drops any non-json tokens and signals a partial/invalid output with a 4xx to the client rather than sending malformed JSON. marco_dev: There's a PR in eng-runtime that adds a framing token between tool and assistant chunks and a strict-json runtime option that fails the stream if non-json text is emitted. Deploy-bot says build started but not yet released. emily.chen: Customer also hit a different edge: when the tool returns nested JSON that contains embedded HTML (from a scraped report), the assistant emits HTML-escaped fragments and that breaks schema validation downstream. raj.patel: Example? Please paste minimal payload. emily.chen: Example tool content: ``` {"policy_notes":"

Approved by compliance

", "actions":[{"name":"notify","payload":"{\"email\":\"ops@acme.com\"}"}]} ``` assistant then emitted: ``` {"result": {"policy": {"status":"ok","notes":"

Approved by compliance

"}, "meta":"Generated at 2026-03-21"}} ``` But sometimes the assistant also wraps JSON fragments in triple-backticks when streaming, e.g. ```{"result":...}``` which breaks the client's json parsing. marco_dev: That's definitely on us. We need two fixes: 1) canonicalize tool outputs so they are raw JSON (no HTML escaping) and 2) runtime strict-json mode that strips markdown/code fences. I'll escalate. raj.patel: Meanwhile sales needs answers: 1) can we get a Dedicated POC price estimate today? 2) ETA on strict-json/runtime fix? 3) Can Security prepare a QSA response template for this customer (they asked for encryption in transit details)? emily.chen: Answers I can provide now: - Pricing: ballpark for 4x A100-equivalent Dedicated eval is $40k/month list, we can give a 25% trial discount for 30 days — will confirm with finance. (subject to seat/license add-ons) - Runtime fix ETA: eng-runtime estimates a canary release in ~72 hours, GA in 10 business days if no regressions. - Security QSA: security asked me to collect specific customer contact info and the questionnaire PDF; I'll forward. sara_ops: Action items: - emily.chen -> confirm pricing and send quote (by EOD). - marco_dev -> post PR link and short mitigation (prompt + SDK filter) in this thread. - raj.patel -> collect customer's questionnaire and contact, loop security. - eng-runtime (cc @marco_dev) -> enable temporary quota bump for Dedicated eval if approved by ops. marco_dev: Mitigation we recommend immediately: 1) Request customer set stream=false (temporary) OR 2) Use system prompt: "STRICT_JSON=true" plus instruct assistant to respond only with JSON (no fences). Example message: `Please output exactly one JSON object; do not include any markdown, code fences, or commentary.` 3) SDK-level: assemble chunks but run a final regex to strip leading/trailing backticks and then validate with json.loads; if invalid, request a retry with stream disabled. Code snippet they used: ``` # pseudo-sdk assemble buf = '' for chunk in stream: buf += chunk['content'] # naive fix buf = re.sub(r"^```+|```+$", "", buf) parsed = json.loads(buf) ``` raj.patel: That regex trick fixed 70% of their cases but not when assistant injects extra text between object members. emily.chen: I'll push the price and the questionnaire now. Marco can you drop the PR link? marco_dev: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/4722 — adds strict-json runtime flag + streaming framing tokens. Not yet deployed. deploy-bot: CI passed: unit-tests: 312, integration: 28/30 (2 flaky tests), will retry. emily.chen: Thanks team. I'll tell the customer the short-term mitigation and ETA. If eng wants, I'll create a joint call this week to shadow their POC so we can reproduce with streaming enabled. raj.patel: Please do. Also cc finance and security on the call invite. emily.chen: Will do. :thumbsup:
